detail.title: Working Conditions in Light of Factory Law Provisions of the Public Sector Enterprises of Bangladesh: A Case Study on Jute Mills
detail.abstract: This study aims to examine the working conditions of public sector jute mills of Bangladesh in light of the existing Factory Law provisions, with a focus on compliance, implementation gaps, and workers' welfare. Using a case study approach, the research analyzes selected state-owned jute mills to assess key aspects of working conditions, including occupational safety and health, working hours, wage practices, sanitation, and welfare facilities as stipulated under the Factories Act 1965. Data were collected through structured questionnaires, in-depth interviews with workers and management, and analysis of relevant policy documents and the published reports. The findings reveal partial compliance with legal provisions, with significant shortcomings in workplace safety, medical facilities, and enforcement mechanisms. Institutional inefficiencies, resource constraints, and weak monitoring systems are identified as major barriers to effective implementation of factory laws. The study suggests the need for stronger regulatory oversight, improved labor-management relations, and policy reforms to ensure decent working conditions in public sector jute mills, contributing to sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh.

title: Contractual Mechanisms for Preventing and Detection of Accounting Fraud in the Governance of Commercial Companies
affiliations: University of Coimbra Institute for Legal Research

detail.title: Contractual Mechanisms for Preventing and Detection of Accounting Fraud in the Governance of Commercial Companies
detail.abstract: Accounting fraud is a governance risk that compromises the reliability of financial reporting, distorts the decisions of shareholders and creditors, and fuels litigation and systemic crises. Based on Article 64 of the Commercial Companies Code and the fiduciary duties of directors, this text analyzes how contractual instruments can function as an "additional layer" of prevention and detection: (i) statutory clauses and shareholder agreements that reinforce duties of information, auditing, and internal control; (ii) covenants in financing agreements that create triggers for reporting and reacting to deviations, with attention to the risk of creditor interference; and (iii) remuneration clauses—deferral, malus, and clawback—that mitigate incentives for manipulation. In a comparative note, the Sarbanes–Oxley Act and the UK Corporate Governance Code 2024 are discussed as relevant references. In addition, a recent European layer (CSRD/ESRS, CSDDD, Whistleblowing Directive, SRD II, and MAR) is integrated, arguing that the EU has reinforced "information-based" governance (standardized reporting and assurance), "by diligence" (due diligence duties in the value chain), and "by market integrity" (disclosure rules and manipulation prevention). It concludes with principles for drafting clauses and legal-corporate limits to avoid "over-governance."

title: Precautionary Diplomacy in the Gulf: Why Iran's Neighbours Chose Restraint Over Escalation

detail.title: Precautionary Diplomacy in the Gulf: Why Iran's Neighbours Chose Restraint Over Escalation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Middle East politics and Iran politics
declarations.funderStatement: Changiz Abbasi political Sociologist and international analyst

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the cautious response of Middle Eastern states to Iran’s internal unrest in 2025–2026, explaining why key regional actors refrained from escalation despite enduring rivalries with Tehran. It argues that Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman and Turkey adopted a strategy of restraint rooted in precautionary diplomacy rather than reconciliation. Faced with the risks of military confrontation, energy disruption and regional spillover, these states prioritised stability and crisis containment over opportunistic gains. The paper situates this behaviour within a realist framework, highlighting how uncertainty and fear of uncontrolled outcomes shaped regional responses. It concludes that, in a volatile Middle Eastern environment, restraint can emerge as a rational strategy even among adversaries.

title: The Cognitive Bandwidth Research Program A Capacity-Centered Framework for Leadership, Organizations, and Ethical System Design
affiliations: Deliberate Evolution Institute

detail.title: The Cognitive Bandwidth Research Program A Capacity-Centered Framework for Leadership, Organizations, and Ethical System Design
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Cognitive Bandwidth Research Program, a multi-paper inquiry into how human cognitive capacity constrains leadership effectiveness, organizational performance, and ethical system design under sustained pressure. Rather than offering prescriptive tools or behavioral frameworks, the program advances a capacity-centered lens that reframes many persistent leadership and performance challenges as consequences of unmanaged cognitive constraint rather than individual deficiency. The research program integrates insights from cognitive science, systems theory, organizational behavior, and applied leadership observation to examine five core dimensions: capacity as a governing constraint, the failure of optimization under pressure, saturation thresholds and collapse dynamics, recovery processes, and the ethical responsibilities of leadership in systems that shape human bandwidth. Together, these papers establish a coherent theoretical foundation for understanding performance, stability, and responsibility in modern organizations without reducing complex human behavior to motivational or cultural explanations.

detail.abstract: This policy framework examines the prerequisites for successful post-conflict reconstruction and democratic transition in the Gaza Strip, drawing systematically upon comparative analysis of international precedents including the United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor (UNTAET), the UN Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK), the Dayton Accords implementation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Northern Ireland peace process. The proposed 36-month implementation framework addresses the extraordinary scale of destruction documented by the World Bank, United Nations, and European Union joint assessment, which estimated total recovery and reconstruction needs at USD 53.2 billion (World Bank et al., 2025). The analysis proceeds from recognition that Gaza's demographic structure-with 68% of the population under age 30 and unemployment reaching 79.7% as of October 2024 (International Labour Organization, 2024)-creates conditions requiring immediate attention to employment generation alongside governance reform. Drawing upon Stedman's (1997) spoiler management framework and the accumulated scholarship on post-conflict institution building, this paper argues that successful transition requires five concurrent elements: sustained international commitment, adequate financial resources, meaningful local ownership, transparent anti-corruption mechanisms, and realistic implementation timelines. The framework proposes phased benchmarks across four implementation periods: stabilization (months 0-6), institution-building (months 6-18), electoral preparation (months 18-30), and democratic transition (months 30-36), while acknowledging that full consolidation requires 10-15 years of sustained engagement. The paper concludes with analysis of principal risks and mitigation strategies, emphasizing that premature withdrawal of international support-as occurred in Afghanistan-represents the primary threat to transition sustainability.

title:
Leadership Cognitive Bandwidth Collapse 
A Capacity-First Model of Leadership and Organizational Performance Under Pressure
affiliations: Deliberate Evolution Institute

detail.title:
Leadership Cognitive Bandwidth Collapse 
A Capacity-First Model of Leadership and Organizational Performance Under Pressure
detail.abstract:
Persistent performance breakdowns in organizations are commonly attributed to deficits in motivation, capability, or culture. However, longitudinal observation across leadership, team, and executive contexts suggests a different underlying mechanism: cognitive bandwidth constriction caused by accumulated and poorly understood forms of load. 
Cognitive bandwidth refers to the finite capacity individuals and systems have to process information, regulate emotion, make decisions, and sustain effective action. When this capacity becomes constrained, behavior often appears irrational, resistant, or disengaged. Traditional interventions tend to misdiagnose these outcomes as personal or cultural failures, leading to optimization efforts that inadvertently increase pressure and accelerate collapse. 
This paper introduces a capacity-first model of leadership and organizational design, grounded in the observation that cognitive bandwidth is influenced by multiple distinct categories of load. These loads operate differently, compound under pressure, and constrain performance through non-linear interactions that are largely invisible to conventional metrics. Importantly, the relevance and dominance of these load categories vary based on context, system design, and environmental pressure. 
Empirical patterns indicate that attempts to optimize performance before addressing underlying load are consistently ineffective. In contrast, environments that prioritize stabilization by reducing unnecessary pressure demonstrate rapid improvements in clarity, decision quality, and functional capacity without requiring personal disclosure, behavioral correction, or motivational techniques.
By emphasizing anonymous pattern recognition and environmental intervention rather than individual diagnosis, this model reframes leadership from a discipline of behavioral influence to one of capacity stewardship. When cognitive bandwidth is protected, many problems resolve without direct intervention. When it is ignored, even high-performing systems eventually destabilize.

title: Redefining Success: A Qur'anic Framework Beyond Material Achievement
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Redefining Success: A Qur'anic Framework Beyond Material Achievement
detail.abstract: Contemporary definitions of success are predominantly shaped by material, economic, and outcome-oriented frameworks, often reducing human achievement to wealth accumulation, status, or external productivity. While these models dominate modern discourse, they frequently overlook deeper questions of purpose, moral alignment, and the full realization of human potential. This paper argues that such reductionist conceptions fail to provide a comprehensive or sustainable understanding of success. Drawing upon the Qur'anic worldview as an epistemological framework, the study proposes an alternative definition of success grounded in alignment with divine purpose rather than material attainment alone. Through conceptual analysis of key Qur'anic notions such as falah (true success), guidance, human agency, and moral responsibility, the paper demonstrates that success in the Qur'anic paradigm is understood as the maximal actualization of God-given capacities within the boundaries of ethical and spiritual alignment. This model reframes success as a process-based and purpose-driven phenomenon, extending beyond temporal outcomes to encompass individual integrity, social responsibility, and trans-temporal accountability. By situating the Qur'anic perspective within broader discussions of human flourishing and development, this study contributes a faith-based yet analytically rigorous framework that challenges prevailing material definitions and invites further interdisciplinary engagement on the meaning of success.

title: "Zakat as an Instrument of Economic Empowerment: Assessing Its Impact on the Economic Resources of Muslim Residents in Zamboanga City, Philippines"

detail.title: "Zakat as an Instrument of Economic Empowerment: Assessing Its Impact on the Economic Resources of Muslim Residents in Zamboanga City, Philippines"
detail.abstract: Considering Zakat is one of the primary principles of Islam, it is not only a spiritual necessity but also a considerable possibility in the context of socioeconomic development. This paper places Zakat in the socioeconomic setting of Zamboanga City where there is significant Muslim population that is actively engaged in different economic activities such as professional services, entrepreneurship, commerce and informal trade. These industries also play a significant role in both formal and informal sectors of the city, as they enhance the aspect in which Muslim communities are being used to promote economic productivity, social stability and inclusive local development. The study is based on a qualitative case study and is conducted among three Muslim families which are actively practicing the concept of giving zakat to their neighbors. In this way, the paper will study the implementation of Zakat at the family level and the operationalization of Zakat as a social redistribution and support mechanism in society. Basing on Islamic ethical principles, the practice of zakat demonstrates the equilibrium between religious duty and empathy in acknowledgment of various abilities and resource endowment of different people. Muslims are urged to volunteer in performing their religious obligations because of the economic struggles as a show of devotion and moral obligation and the teachings of Islam allow some leniency to meet human constraints. First of all, the results obtained indicate that zakat is a religious practice that enhances religious adherence and, at the same time, fosters social welfare, resilience of communities, and simultaneously a sense of socioeconomic development in Zamboanga City.

title: Tractor Supply Company: Living Life Out Here
affiliations: University of Virginia - Darden School of Business and University of Virginia - Darden School of Business

detail.title: Tractor Supply Company: Living Life Out Here
detail.abstract:
Tractor Supply Company (TSC) had benefited in surprising ways from the COVID-19 pandemic, most notably from household migration to rural areas and a shift in consumption habits toward the self-reliant, outdoor-centered lifestyle at the core of its business model. In mid-February of 2023, CEO Hal Lawton had good reason to be pleased with company's recent performance. A particular point of pride was how TSC had been able to both fund growth and make generous payouts to shareholders. However, favorable market trends had run their course, and growth was likely to slow. Margins might even tighten. The key question in the case is whether the company's stated goals, which included an increase in dividends and only modest pullback on repurchases, were achievable in light of company guidance on sales and margins. More importantly, student analysis builds familiarity with the construction of integrated financial statements, comfort with the execution of sensitivity analyses, and understanding of cash flow components and drivers. This field-based case functions equally well as an introduction to forecasting and as a platform for a deep dive into sensitivity analysis and performance drivers. At the University of Virginia Darden School of Business, it has been used in a first-year class on financial forecasting in the core curriculum, as well as in executive programs to drive discussions about firm-level strategic choices with respect to payout policies and investment.

Excerpt

Tractor Supply Company: Living Life Out Here

Contemplating the financial condition of Tractor Supply Company (TSC) in mid-February of 2023, CEO Hal Lawton had plenty of reasons to be excited. TSC had benefited in surprising ways from the COVID-19 pandemic—most notably from the migration of households to rural areas and their embrace of a self-reliant, outdoor-centered lifestyle. The needs of these new customers were easily accommodated alongside TSC's traditional customers, who were often described as recreational farmers and ranchers. The new customer mix prompted TSC's “Life Out Here” strategy, which included improving stores (under the name Project Fusion), adding garden centers, and expanding the company's Neighbor's Club loyalty program.

Reflecting on the past year and the year ahead, which would mark the company's 85th year in business, Lawton observed that “Tractor Supply had another remarkable year in 2022 as we continued to gain market share and advance our strategic initiatives.” The evidence was clear. Revenue growth, which reached 30% in 2020 and 20% in 2021 as a result of pandemic-induced buying, had moderated in 2022 but remained strong at close to 12%. Margins remained above pre-COVID levels, and payouts to shareholders in the form of dividends and repurchases increased to over $1.1 billion. Lawton went on to note that “in just over two years since introducing our Life Out Here strategy, we have executed Project Fusion in nearly 30% of our store base, built more than 300 garden centers, expanded our digital and supply chain capabilities, and grown our Neighbor's Club membership 47% to more than 28 million members.” He concluded that “our future couldn't be brighter.” Analysts who followed the company clearly shared that optimism. Many rated the company as a buy despite the fact that TSC had already substantially outperformed a variety of benchmarks. Typical of sentiment at the time was a February 2, 2023, Credit Suisse report that stated boldly that “Life Out Here” was “Here to Stay.” The report set a target price of $260 a share when the prior day's closing price was about $230.

TSC was clear about its near-term financial goals. The company had reiterated a fiscal-year-2023 outlook that predicted revenues would reach over $15 billion, operating margin would land between 10.1% and 10.3%, and capital expenditures could reach $775 million. At the same time, the company was committed to share repurchases of at least $575 million on top of its planned dividend. These were not particularly ambitious goals relative to 2022, but the market was not without headwinds and companies typically exceeded their targets. Investors would certainly wonder whether these goals could all be achieved, where any opportunities to exceed expectations might arise, and what TSC might prioritize if things got tight.

detail.title: Bretton Woods and the Financial Crisis of 1971 (A) and (B) (Abridged) (CHINESE)
detail.abstract:
This is a Chinese translation of the July, 21, 2020 version of UVA-F-1837. In August 1971, US President Richard Nixon must decide how to respond to a growing “run” on the US dollar. Declining confidence in the dollar has led some national trading partners to redeem dollars for gold at the US Treasury's gold window. Nixon has convened an urgent conference with his economic advisers at Camp David to consider a response. The two dominant policy alternatives are (a) gradual intervention proposed by central banker, Arthur Burns; and (b) “shock treatment” (devaluation of the dollar by abandoning the commitment under the Bretton Woods Agreement to convert dollars into gold at the rate of $35/ounce) proposed by Treasury Secretary John Connally. The task for the student is to assess the situation and recommend a course of action. The A case describes the Bretton Woods system, the run on the dollar, and Nixon's policy dilemma. The B case gives the text of Nixon's 1971 address outlining his New Economic Policy. This A and B abridged case, which has been taught successfully in Darden in-person and online classes, shortens the total presentation by eliminating some of the quoted material; the student task in this case is to analyze Nixon's decision and decide on next steps. The C case presents a brief epilogue.

title: Assessing The Financial Limitations On Project Implementation In Ngos A Case Study Of Family Planning
affiliations: Independent and DMI-St John the Baptist University, Malawi

detail.title: Assessing The Financial Limitations On Project Implementation In Ngos A Case Study Of Family Planning
detail.abstract: This article investigates the pervasive challenge of financial limitations in Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) project implementation, using the Family Planning Association of Malawi (FPAM) as an in-depth case study. Framed by Resource Dependency Theory (RDT), the research employs a qualitative methodology including semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, and document analysis to explore how donor dependency shapes operational realities. Findings reveal financial constraints, manifesting as insufficient funding, delayed disbursements, and restrictive donor conditions, critically disrupt project planning, compromise service quality, and undermine community trust. While FPAM employs reactive coping strategies like cost-cutting and donor negotiation, these are insufficient for fostering long-term resilience. The article identifies a consequential power imbalance inherent in the donor-recipient relationship, which limits organizational autonomy and strategic alignment with local needs. It concludes by proposing a multi-stakeholder framework for action, advocating for enhanced internal financial governance, strategic diversification of funding, donor policy reform towards flexibility, and stronger local partnerships. This study contributes context-specific evidence to the literature on NGO management in resource-constrained settings and offers pragmatic pathways from financial vulnerability towards sustainable impact.

title: Participatory Budgeting in Richmond
affiliations: University of Virginia - Darden School of Business, University of Virginia - Darden School of Business and University of Virginia - Darden School of Business

detail.title: Participatory Budgeting in Richmond
detail.abstract:
Set in November 2023, this case asks students to take the perspective of Matthew Slaats, a consultant for the city of Richmond, Virginia, as he selects a voting rule for the city's new participatory budgeting (PB) program. PB allows voters to determine how to allocate a portion of the city's budget to a select list of projects. Most PB programs use approval voting, a rule that allows participants to vote for an unlimited number of projects. After voting concludes, the projects are ranked based on the number of votes they receive, and they are funded based on those rankings until the PB budget is exhausted. As he helps Richmond create its PB program, Slaats must decide whether to recommend approval voting or a different voting rule. To inform his decision, he plans to evaluate data from Ursynów, Poland, which used approval voting for its PB process. If his analysis reveals that approval voting disproportionately favors certain project categories, neighborhoods, or demographic groups, he may wish to suggest a different voting rule. Students receive a supplementary Excel file containing the Ursynów data, and they must analyze the data to complete the assignment. Notably, the case can facilitate a robust discussion even if students use generative AI tools, as the core aspects of the case decision all require human judgment. At the Darden School of Business, this case has been taught in the first-year core MBA “Decision Analysis” course, in an elective course on how to prepare students for data-intensive roles, and in an executive education program on data analytics. It can be used in MBA-level or executive education courses on quantitative analysis, data visualization, or data-driven decision-making.

Excerpt

Participatory Budgeting in Richmond

In November 2023, Matthew Slaats prepared for a meeting with the city council of Richmond, Virginia. Slaats, an independent consultant for the city of Richmond, was helping the city create a participatory budgeting (PB) program. A Richmond city councillor had initially contacted Slaats about PB in 2018, and after more than five years of conversations, deliberations, and debates, the city planned to launch the initiative in summer 2024. However, Slaats and the city council still had to decide on several elements of the program, including the process for determining which PB projects to fund.

PB enabled residents to collectively decide how to allocate a portion of the city budget. The typical process was for residents to vote on a set of predetermined projects, after which a voting rule translated the votes into an overall ranking of projects, with the highest-ranked projects receiving funding. Most PB systems used a rule called approval voting to determine which projects to fund. Approval voting enabled participants to vote for as many projects as they wanted. Each vote carried equal weight: The value of a vote did not decline if the person who cast it also voted for other projects. At the end of the voting process, the PB organizers tallied the votes and ranked the projects based on the number of votes they had received. The organizers then funded the projects, beginning with those that received the most votes and proceeding down the list until they had exhausted the budget. Project cost did not factor into the voting system or the funding process, except insofar as more expensive projects exhausted the budget faster than cheaper ones. This method appeared fair, but Slaats worried that it could prompt the program to overspend on categories or projects that favored some demographic groups over others.

The city council hoped that the PB program would invest in neighborhoods that had historically received insufficient city funding. They also wanted the program to improve community engagement, envisioning it as a way to encourage Richmond's residents to participate in the democratic process. However, if the PB initiative consistently failed to fund certain categories, Slaats knew that the voters who supported those projects might eventually lose interest in the program.

When Kazuo Ueda took the reins as governor of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) in April 2023, he signaled that he would continue the ultra-loose monetary policy that had characterized Japan's central bank for over a decade. 考虑到影响宏观经济的诸多复杂因素，很难准确评估安倍经济学在多大程度上实现了其目标。但安倍所在的自由民主党自 2012 年以来持续执政，暗示着安倍经济学议程获得了广泛支持。植田深刻意识到安倍经济学的受欢迎程度，他谨慎地传递出信号：即使领导层更迭，日本央行的货币政策方针将保持稳定。

title: 50 Years Of Bangladesh-China Ties: Trade, Infrastructure Investment Underpin The Relationship

detail.title: 50 Years Of Bangladesh-China Ties: Trade, Infrastructure Investment Underpin The Relationship
detail.abstract: China and Bangladesh celebrated 50 years of diplomatic relations. On October 4, leaders from both nations, including President Xi Jinping and President Mohammed Shahabuddin, exchanged congratulatory messages. They highlighted a partnership built on mutual respect and "win-win cooperation." An academic way to view this partnership is through the theory of liberalism. In international relations, liberalism is seen as a progressive idea. It argues that countries are not always in conflict; instead, they can cooperate for mutual benefit. Liberalism states that economic ties and international agreements build trust. This cooperation leads to shared growth and lasting peace. It is a "win-win" situation, not a "zero-sum" game where one side must lose for the other to win. The foundation of the relationship is based on these liberal principles. Both nations adhere to the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence. These include mutual respect for sovereignty and non-interference in internal affairs. This diplomatic groundwork allows for a pragmatic partnership. It is not based on shared political ideology. It is based on shared interests in development and stability. This creates a positive-sum game, where both sides can win. The engine of this "win-win" relationship is economic interdependence. Liberal theory states that when countries trade heavily, the cost of conflict becomes too high. China is Bangladesh's largest trading partner. In the 2023-2024 fiscal year, bilateral trade was significant, even if imbalanced. Bangladesh imported goods worth $16.64 billion from China. This massive trade volume links the two economies closely. Bangladesh depends on China for machinery, chemicals, and textiles for its vital ready-made garment (RMG) industry. China sees Bangladesh as a major and growing market. This deep economic tie creates a powerful incentive for peace.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the effects of forward guidance and unconventional monetary policy on financial and macro-economic variables using euro area data. I decompose intra-daily variation in response to communication by the ECB Governing Council using sign-restrictions, with the key identifying assumption being whether expansionary communication shocks steepen the yield curve (a forward guidance shock) or flatten it (a spread compression shock). Central bank “information shocks” are extracted via an additional restriction on equities. I employ recently developed non-parametric estimation methods to estimate a medium-scale time-varying parameter SVAR model with high-frequency identification, allowing consideration of multiple transmission channels simultaneously. Expansionary spread compression shocks markedly reduce volatility and persistently lower spreads, and affect activity and prices in line with theory. Spread compression surprises affect macro-economic variables in a manner comparable to forward guidance surprises. The effects of both forward guidance and yield curve compression surprises on inflation increased in the post-European sovereign debt crisis period, as did their effect on unemployment.

title: “It Doesn't Necessarily mean Money to Me”: Definitions of Adulthood and Perceptions of Success among Former Participants in a Youth Leadership Program

detail.title: “It Doesn't Necessarily mean Money to Me”: Definitions of Adulthood and Perceptions of Success among Former Participants in a Youth Leadership Program
detail.abstract: The transition to adulthood for young people today has become more complicated and drawn out compared to previous generations. But we currently know very little about how young people themselves define adulthood or a successful life. While the dearth of research on subjective views of adulthood is remarkable in light of rapidly changing societal contexts, it is particularly concerning with regard to young people who are structurally excluded from the means to achieve traditional markers of adulthood, such as finishing school and entry into the labor market. What is more, subjective notions of adult status or success embody key dimensions of young peoples agency because they guide decision-making during their transition to adulthood. Deepening our understanding of how disadvantaged youth define adulthood could provide much needed nuance to our knowledge about their experiences and offer important implications for youth programming. Based on 55 qualitative interviews with former participants of an intensive youth leadership program, this paper explores subjective definitions of adulthood and success. While these definitions continued to include traditional markers such as educational attainment and career success, our respondents also drew on non-traditional notions such as happiness or a more universal sense of stability as indicative of being an adult. We discuss potential implications for future research and youth programming.

detail.abstract: The paper examines the harmonization of administrative judicial powers across the European Union, specifically focusing on the capacity of courts to amend executive decisions. The author’s central thesis posits that EU Member States are legally and practically converging toward a model of active judicial review, driven by the jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the EU and the necessity to safeguard fundamental individual rights under Article 47 of the Charter. Through a comparative legal analysis of the French model alongside recent reforms in Austria and Hungary, the study argues that administrative courts must possess the authority to decide cases on their merits—replacing agency decisions when necessary—rather than merely annulling them. Based on these findings, the author recommends that Polish legislators adapt national acts to explicitly grant these powers, contending that such judicial intervention is essential for the administration of justice and does not violate the principle of separation of powers.

title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Equipment With Multi-Modal Degradation Based on Multi-Scale Similarity Matching

detail.title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Equipment With Multi-Modal Degradation Based on Multi-Scale Similarity Matching
detail.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of industrial equipment is a core component of predictive maintenance, and its accuracy directly affects equipment reliability management and maintenance decision-making. Under multi-fault-mode and complex operating conditions, existing approaches often struggle to achieve both stable fault mode identification and accurate, robust RUL prediction simultaneously. To address this issue, this paper proposes an RUL prediction method that integrates Health Index (HI) construction, fault mode identification, and multi-scale similarity matching. First, an autoencoder (AE) is employed to learn reconstruction features from healthy operating data, enabling the construction of an HI that is sensitive to degradation evolution while maintaining strong robustness. Subsequently, a time-series representation learning framework based on Temporal and Contextual Contrasting (TS-TCC) is adopted to achieve unsupervised fault mode identification, whereby only degradation trajectories belonging to the same fault mode are selected as reference samples. Finally, a multi-scale matching mechanism consisting of short-term scale, full-life-cycle scale, and focal scale is developed. Mean-Residual Comparison (MRC), Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), and Spherical-weighted DTW (SW-DTW) distances are respectively employed to perform differentiated similarity measurements at different scales. In addition, a sliding-threshold strategy is introduced to dynamically activate focal-scale matching, allowing accurate characterization of local fluctuations, global degradation trends, and critical degradation stages. Experimental results on the multi-fault C-MAPSS dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional approaches in terms of prediction accuracy, stability, and adaptability to multiple fault modes, thereby validating the effectiveness and engineering applicability of the proposed framework.

detail.abstract: We study players' engagement decisions with different game modes in a popular multi-generational franchise video game. Some game modes are competitive where players' utility might derive from performance, whereas other game modes are casual and feature the aspect of social interactions with other players. Model-free data patterns suggest that three potential mechanisms could jointly determine players' decisions to engage in competitive versus casual game mode: unobserved preference heterogeneity, learning about their preferences for different modes, and skill accumulation. We develop a novel model that explains players' decisions along both the extensive and the intensive margins with respect to different modes, while incorporating all three mechanisms. These mechanisms can be separately identified in our data set due to the panel feature of the multi-generational game. Our estimation results show several key insights about each mechanism. First, playing the competitive mode accumulates skills much faster than the casual mode. In addition, we find that 27% of the players are inherently more competitive, and accumulate skills much faster by playing the competitive mode more often. Thus, these players spend more time playing and learn about their true preferences faster than others. Building on these insights, we propose several implementable game mode related actions for the managers to improve player engagement along the extensive and intensive margins. For example, introducing a new game mode with competitive features improves players' extensive margins more effectively (by 15∼32%), while a new game mode with casual features improves players' intensive margins more effectively (by 20∼28%).

detail.abstract: Many utilities have provided financial incentives to encourage residential customers to enroll in direct load control (DLC) programs to harness demand response resources. However, financial incentives do not always result in a high participation rate. This study aims to assess residential customers' willingness to enroll in utility-run DLC programs and analyze how incentives affect participation intention. A survey employing the contingent valuation method collected 591 responses from a random sample of U.S. Midwest residents. We prompted a dichotomous choice question to some respondents on whether to enroll in a DLC program with payments ranging from $10-$200, while asking others' participation intention without mentioning a financial incentive. Overall, 57.4% of residents were willing to enroll, and the estimated willingness to accept DLC was $10-$42 per year. We found a U-shaped pattern between payment and willingness to participate, which suggests the intrinsic motivations for DLC participation can be crowded out by monetary incentives. Our analysis estimated the crowded-out intrinsic motivations valued at $30-$157 annually, varied by program type. Additionally, we found several factors affecting acceptance of DLC programs, including knowledge learning, concerns of comfort loss, and personal perception of demand response for energy savings, reliability, and environmental benefits. Findings from this study have significant policy implications and help improve the design of utility DLC programs.

detail.abstract: E-commerce has become one of Vietnam's most dynamic and fastest-growing sectors, reshaping consumer purchasing behavior in the digital economy. This study investigates the key determinants of consumers' trust and its mediating role in online purchase decisions in Vietnam. Primary data were collected through an online survey of 419 Vietnamese consumers who had made at least one purchase on major e-commerce platforms (e.g., Shopee, TikTok, Facebook) during the previous six months. This sampling frame ensured that all respondents had recent and relevant experience with online shopping in Vietnam's e-commerce market. Data were collected between October 2024 and August 2025 using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.1. The findings reveal that website quality (β = 0.235, p < 0.01), reference groups (β = 0.209, p < 0.01), perceived service quality (β = 0.184, p < 0.01), and information security (β = 0.171, p < 0.01) significantly enhance Vietnamese consumers' trust in online shopping. Suppliers' reputation (β = 0.106, p < 0.01) and suppliers' size (β = 0.067, p < 0.01) indirectly strengthen consumers' trust through website quality and perceived service quality, respectively. The study further confirms that trust serves as an essential mediating construct, meaningfully strengthening online purchase decisions among Vietnamese consumers (β = 0.608, p < 0.01). These findings underscore the central importance of trust in shaping consumer behavior in emerging e-commerce markets, indicating that enhancing website quality, improving service reliability, and strengthening data protection can contribute to more sustainable online purchasing behavior among Vietnamese consumers.

Rational Valuation or Herd Behaviour?
detail.abstract: Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) rarely occur evenly over time. Instead, capital markets experience distinct periods of heightened IPO activity, commonly referred to as IPO waves. Traditional financial theory attributes these waves to favourable macroeconomic conditions and rational market timing by firms. However, the growing influence of retail investors, abundant liquidity, and behavioural biases raises an important question: are IPO waves driven by rational valuation or by investor sentiment and herd behaviour? This paper examines the relationship between IPO waves and market sentiment, focusing on whether periods of intense IPO activity coincide with optimistic market conditions and whether such IPOs deliver sustainable long-term performance. Using market return trends, volatility indicators, and post-IPO performance patterns, the study finds that IPO waves are strongly associated with bullish sentiment and subdued risk perception, but are followed by relatively weaker long-term returns. The findings suggest that IPO waves are largely sentiment-driven rather than purely fundamental, highlighting persistent inefficiencies in equity markets.

detail.abstract: Influencer marketing has become a major tool for brands to communicate with consumers, especially in digital advertising. However, its rapid growth has raised questions about whether it genuinely builds consumer trust or simply creates a perception of credibility. This study explores the role of influencer marketing in shaping trust, focusing on the Indian beauty industry. The research compares two brands-Dots & Key and Lakmé-that use different influencer marketing strategies. A qualitative research approach is used, relying on case study and content analysis of publicly available influencer campaigns, brand messaging, and audience interactions. The findings show that Dots & Key's micro-influencer strategy is more effective in creating a sense of authenticity and trust through relatable content and transparent communication. In contrast, Lakmé's celebrity-driven approach builds credibility through aspirational appeal and brand authority rather than personal connection. The study concludes that trust in influencer marketing is increasingly influenced by relatability, transparency, and engagement, not just influencer popularity. These insights highlight the importance of choosing influencer strategies that support long-term consumer trust in a competitive digital market.

detail.abstract: UK universities have become increasingly reliant on international postgraduate recruitment, particularly from South Asian markets such as India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. At the same time, digital search has emerged as the dominant gateway through which prospective students discover and evaluate marketing degree programmes. This article examines whether changes in course naming introduce a category error that reduces search visibility, student comprehension, and enrolment outcomes. Drawing on marketing science literature on category formation, consumer search behaviour, and signalling theory, the study develops and tests a keyword alignment framework using a mixed methods case study of a London based marketing degree programme. Quantitative keyword modelling using Google Trends, Google Keyword Planner, and SEMrush, alongside survey data from prospective students, indicates that programme titles misaligned with dominant search categories experience substantially lower discoverability and weaker perceived employability. The findings suggest that course naming should be treated as a strategic, search informed marketing decision rather than a purely academic classification exercise, particularly in volatile international recruitment markets.

detail.title: Measuring Allocator Performance in Private Capital: Commitment-Level Public Market Equivalent
detail.abstract: We introduce Commitment-Level Public Market Equivalent (CPME), a performance measure for private capital that addresses a fundamental flaw in the widely used KS-PME. KS-PME measures manager skill conditional on capital being deployed. CPME measures allocator skill conditional on capital being committed. This distinction matters because allocators commit capital, not cash flows. Uncalled capital implicitly earns index returns until deployment, creating an opportunity cost that KS-PME ignores. CPME corrects this by measuring performance at the commitment level rather than the deployment level. The result is a metric that is robust to cash flow labeling, stable for young funds, and economically aligned with the allocator's decision problem. We show that CPME is not merely an alternative to KS-PME but the correct measure for strategic asset allocation questions. Both measures agree directionally, but CPME provides more conservative and reliable assessments by properly accounting for uncommitted capital.

detail.abstract: To many disappointed recruits, Multi-Level Marketing (MLM), also known as Networking Marketing (NM), seemed to be the answer to their financial problems. Epixel, an MLM software company listed the top 100 MLM companies in 2023, and four of them were founded before 1981. Furthermore, on average, the income of the top five companies increased by 3.2%. Thus, just like Bitcoin (BTC) in the crypto space, MLM has stood the test of time. In essence, many companies are now embracing the concept of MLM to some extent. However, the same blooming industry has been the breeding ground of many financial scandals recently, particularly in the crypto space. The use of MLM in the digital world is gaining tremendous momentum, mainly because it does not involve the selling of physical products. Furthermore, everyone is looking for an opportunity to make extra income, thereby making MLM very lucrative in the crypto space, particularly in Africa where poverty and inequality levels are significantly high. Thus, the main objectives of this study were to (1) elaborate the shortcomings of the current MLM compensation plans, (2) discuss the core principles to be incorporated in a downline centered compensation plan (DCCP) structure, (3) develop a new DCCP structure, and 4) propose new bonuses under the new DCCP structure. It was found that all the current compensation plans put are upline distributor (sponsor/recruiter) centered (UDC), instead of being downline distributor centered (DDC). The core principles used to develop the new compensation plan were derived from society, business world, and nature. The developed DCCP structure has a tree shape, a significant step towards addressing the current tainted pyramid shape. Additional bonusses under the proposed DCCP include mentoring bonus, deep root discount, wide root/wide branch bonus, thumps up bonus, oxygen champion bonus, renewal discount, preferred upline bonus, and thank you bonus.

detail.title: Perceived Market Risk in New Ventures: A Study of Early-Phase Business Angel Investment Screening
detail.abstract: Business angels are vital sources of funding for new ventures. Yet, acquiring business angel support is difficult. Typically organized in professional networks, business angels collectively evaluate and deliberate about new ventures to determine their worthiness of support. One factor deemed to be critical during this evaluation is market risk. Yet, limited research in Macromarketing examines market risk. To our knowledge, no previous study examines market risk in capital markets, nor do they study angel financing. Neglecting to study angel financing is particularly problematic for macromarketing because this type of finance is much more prominent than venture capital in supporting new ventures. To fill this gap, we begin by exploring the literature by Lusch (and coauthors) linking marketing and capital markets as well as studies of market risk. We then craft fictitious angel investment proposals to measure market risk assessments by business angels and entrepreneurs. We ask which factors impact market risk during the early-phases of the investment screening process (when market risk is weighted more heavily) and identify whether these factors are evaluated differently by entrepreneurs versus business angels. Our findings reveal that commercialization capability, technological compatibility, and intellectual property rights enforceability influence perceived market risk and that entrepreneurs and business angels view these factors significantly differently. We then offer directions for further research related to this study and other work of Lusch. Finally, we suggest practical implications for use by business angels and entrepreneurs.

title: The Sanitisation of Multi-Level Marketing and its effectiveness in African Crypto Trading
affiliations: Mirracle Consultants

detail.title: The Sanitisation of Multi-Level Marketing and its effectiveness in African Crypto Trading
detail.abstract: As stated by Steve Jobs, the dots can only be connected by looking backwards, and not forward. The beginning of commerce can be traced back to the beginning of civilisation, and in those days, people relied on each other for information on products and/or services available at the time. Thus, the concept of network marketing (NM) can be traced back to the inception of civilisation. However, people were not rewarded for sharing information about products and/or services. With the passage of time, sales teams were organised, and businesses started to appreciate the importance of a vibrant salesforce. Consequently, this appreciation led to the establishment of businesses that relied solely of sales reps, also known as agents or canvassers. This necessitated the use of the multi-level marketing (MLM) business model. Today, the MLM industry is a multi-billion-dollar industry, thereby attracting many new start-up businesses to embrace this business model. One industry that has significantly embraced the MLM business model is the crypto assets (CAs) industry, particularly in the crypto trading (CT) area. However, the MLM business model has been tainted over the past years because of various reasons. Hence, the main objectives of this study are to 1) restore the reputation of the MLM business model, 2) and to determine its effectiveness in African CT. From the results, it was found that NM is at the heart of MLM, and many large businesses have once employed or are using NM to increase awareness and/or sales. Regarding its effectiveness in African CT, it was found that the use of the MLM business model in CT enhances investment, employment, and entrepreneurship opportunities in the crypto space.

title: Influence of Green Marketing Factors on Green Purchase Intention and Consumption Behavior in Kathmandu

detail.title: Influence of Green Marketing Factors on Green Purchase Intention and Consumption Behavior in Kathmandu

publicationDetails.detailsText: SOMTU Journal of Business and Management Research, volume 3, issue 1, 2026[10.3126/sjbmr.v3i1.91059]

detail.abstract: This research aims to understand the impact of green marketing factors on green purchase intention and purchase behavior, particularly examining how green product quality, green value, and perceived consumer effectiveness influence purchase intentions and consumption behavior in Kathmandu Metropolitan City. In this study, causal research is used, and data is gathered from 287 consumers through convenience sampling via Google Forms. A 7-point Likert scale was applied, and the data were analyzed using Smart PLS with Structural Equation Modeling. Findings show that green purchase intention, green value, and perceived consumer effectiveness have a positive and significant impact on green consumption behavior. Similarly, green product quality, green value, and perceived consumer effectiveness significantly influence green purchase intention. However, there is a positive but not significant relationship between green product quality and green consumption behavior. Results further show that green purchase intention fully mediates the relationship between green product quality and green consumption behavior but partially mediates the relationship between green value and perceived consumer effectiveness with green consumption behavior. It concludes with the importance of aligning green marketing strategies with consumer values and selfefficacy, while policymakers should invest in education and awareness to foster consumer belief in the effectiveness of individual action.

title: The Illusion of Calorie Fluency: How Metacognitive Uncertainty Leads to Less Extreme Healthiness Perceptions of Foods
affiliations: Texas Tech University - Rawls College of Business and Goizueta Business School

detail.title: The Illusion of Calorie Fluency: How Metacognitive Uncertainty Leads to Less Extreme Healthiness Perceptions of Foods
detail.abstract: Calorie information is frequently displayed in retail settings where food items are purchased, including grocery stores, hypermarkets, restaurants, cafés, convenience stores, and specialty shops. Some types of retailers are legally required to display calorie counts on packaging, menus, or menu boards. Conventional wisdom suggests that as people become more exposed to calorie information, they will make more informed choices and will be better able to judge the healthiness of foods. This research proposes a more nuanced influence of calorie information on consumers' food evaluations. Specifically, this research hypothesizes that consumers are often overly confident in their ability to use calories to evaluate foods, an illusory fluency that is likely the result of the ubiquity of calorie information. Consistent with this illusory fluency account, this research finds that when consumers attempt to use calorie information in an evaluation or estimation task, the result can create metacognitive uncertainty, resulting in more moderate (i.e., less extreme) evaluations of the healthiness of foods. After trying to utilize their calorie knowledge in judgments or evaluations, consumers subsequently evaluate unhealthy foods as healthier, and healthy foods as less healthy. Nine experiments support the prediction that metacognitive uncertainty in the usage of calorie information in judgments can lead to more moderate evaluations of the healthiness of foods, and less healthy food choices.

detail.abstract: We develop a microsimulation model that can identify Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) as financially distressed due to their inability to meet short term losses with cash (liquidity distress) or to meet their debt repayments (solvency distress). We estimate that – on these metrics – around one-in-six Irish SMEs may have been financially distressed at the end of 2020, or 14 per cent when weighted by debt balances. The model can be used for policy assessment: we calibrate the model to fiscal support implemented in Ireland during the first three quarters of 2020 and estimate that it reduced the share of distressed SME debt by two-fifths. On targeting, we show that a hypothetical scheme selecting firms with the smallest losses first could reduce distress rates from 19 to 7 per cent – albeit we do not suggest this is the welfare-optimising approach. On policy design, we show that debt-based support schemes reduce distress rates by less than grants, and this is driven by the greater role played by solvency over liquidity concerns in a debt-based support regime.

title: Entrepreneurial Branding, Psychology, and Social Media-Driven Market Sustainability
affiliations: and Independent Researcher

detail.title: Entrepreneurial Branding, Psychology, and Social Media-Driven Market Sustainability
detail.abstract: The growing dominance of social media has reshaped how entrepreneurs construct brands, engage audiences, and sustain market presence. This study examines the intersection of entrepreneurial branding and psychological processes in driving market sustainability through social media platforms. Drawing on perspectives on identity formation and psychological branding, the paper explores how entrepreneurs strategically present personal and business identities to build trust, emotional connection, and long-term consumer relationships. The study highlights the role of psychological factors, including authenticity, self-presentation, and perceived credibility, in enhancing audience engagement and reinforcing brand resilience. Using a conceptual and empirical approach, the findings demonstrate that social media-driven branding is not merely a promotional activity but a strategic mechanism that supports adaptability, competitiveness, and sustainability in dynamic digital markets. The study contributes to entrepreneurship and digital marketing literature by integrating psychological branding with social media strategy, offering insights for entrepreneurs seeking sustainable growth in platform-based economies.

title: Tokenization Won’t Rewrite the Time Value of Money — But It Will Reprice Risk
affiliations: Fintech Founder

detail.title: Tokenization Won’t Rewrite the Time Value of Money — But It Will Reprice Risk
detail.abstract: This paper argues that tokenization, real-time settlement, and modern payment infrastructure do not alter the time value of money. Instead, they reduce market and operational frictions that investors price as risk premia embedded in discount rates. We outline the Tokenized Valuation Pathway™ (TVP™), a finance-first causal chain linking settlement infrastructure improvements to risk-premia compression, discount-rate adjustments, and intrinsic value changes. The framework is technology-agnostic and grounded in asset-pricing and market-microstructure theory.

title: Electronic Health Record (E.H.R) Management System Project

detail.title: Electronic Health Record (E.H.R) Management System Project
detail.abstract: An Electronic Health Record (EHR) is an evolving concept defined as a systematic collection of electronic health information about individual patients or populations. It is a record in digital format that is theoretically capable of being shared across different health care settings and it include a range of data like demographics, medical history, medication and allergies, immunization status, laboratory test results, radiology images, vital signs, personal statistics like age and weight, and more. In many cases this sharing can occur by way of network-connected enterprise-wide information systems and other information networks or exchanges. The healthcare community generally agrees that improved use of accurate, current, and clearly understood health information is essential to the delivery of high-quality, cost-effective healthcare. The benefits of this include improved clinical documentation and customer service, more efficient clinical workflows, improved medication management, and reduced transcription and labor costs .The healthcare industry has traditionally underutilized technology as a means of improving the delivery of patient care. Even today, organizations still rely on paper medical records and handwritten notes to inform and make decisions. Digital information is collated and kept between departments and applications, making access to a patient's longitudinal record difficult, if not impossible .

title: Tax Expenditures and Behavioural Responses: The Case of Duty-free Exemptions

detail.abstract: Tax expenditures are the losses in revenue from exempting parts of the tax base from taxation. The conventional method for computing tax expenditures disregards behavioural effects. Using an empirically based demand model, we simulate two reform scenarios that repeal current tax expenditures related to on-arrival duty-free sales of alcohol and tobacco in Norway. The model includes both recorded and unrecorded consumption, tracking all demand responses and their impacts on the tax base. Our results suggest that incorporating these behavioural effects reduces tax expenditures calculated by the conventional approach by more than one third.

title: Predictive Models of Solar Generation in the Microgrid
affiliations: Institute of General Energy of NAS of Ukraine and Institute of General Energy of NAS of Ukraine

detail.title: Predictive Models of Solar Generation in the Microgrid
detail.abstract: This chapter presents a comprehensive analysis of predictive models for forecasting solar generation in microgrids, with a focus on optimizing energy management for systems supporting electric vehicle charging stations. Various methodologies are examined, including simple exponential smoothing (SESM and its variant SESM‑2), seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), regression‐based approaches (linear, ridge, and lasso), the ensemble random forest method, and advanced deep-learning techniques such as long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. Forecast performance is evaluated through error metrics–MAE, RMSE, and R2–and benchmarking against average base values. While simpler models like SESM‑2 deliver fast implementation and low computational overhead, their limited ability to capture seasonality and abrupt weather changes reduces accuracy under dynamic conditions. In contrast, the SARIMA and regression models capture periodic trends but may struggle with transient fluctuations. The LSTM model excels by handling long-term dependencies and complex nonlinearities, achieving the highest precision. These insights offer practical guidelines for selecting forecasting tools tailored to specific operational demands, ensuring enhanced reliability and resilience in microgrid operations.

title: Do Currency Markets Anticipate Equity Volatility?

detail.title: Do Currency Markets Anticipate Equity Volatility?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The research was conducted independently and without influence from any external organization.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available financial market data and does not involve human participants, personal data, or identifiable subjects. As such, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: With daily and weekly log returns for the years 2007-2025, we assess the impact of a tradable VIX (VXX) proxy ETF on currency ETFs that include U.S. dollar (UUP), Japanese yen (FXY), Euro (FXE), Swiss franc (FXF), and Australian dollar (FXA). We perform coincident correlations, lead-lag correlation sweeps, and Granger causality tests to test two competing hypotheses. Whether foreign exchange markets act as a leading indicator of equity volatility, or whether both respond contemporaneously to common risk shocks. We discover no evidence that foreign exchange currency markets systematically lead equity volatility at either daily or weekly frequencies. In the tested currencies, the strongest relationships with volatility occur contemporaneously, with lead-lag effects clustering at zero. Granger causality tests further reveal that shocks to volatility more often precede currency movements than the reverse. These results indicate that currencies operate as confirmation mechanisms for risk regimes, rather than as predictive timing tools. While FX movements are unsuitable for short-horizon volatility forecasting, their polarity (e.g. Yen strength and Australian dollar weakness) remains useful for validating broader risk-off environments within systematic and algorithmic trading setups.

title: Forecast Combination for Tail Risk with Regulator-Aware Decision Trees
affiliations: Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Erasmus School of Economics (ESE) and University of Birmingham - Department of Economics

detail.title: Forecast Combination for Tail Risk with Regulator-Aware Decision Trees
detail.abstract: In this paper, we address the challenge of combining forecasts for Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) by employing nonparametric weights which are functions of macro-financial state variables. We develop a tailor-made, tree-based machine learning procedure in which optimal combination weights remain constant within economic regimes but vary across them. The continuously varying regimes themselves are identified in a fully data-driven manner. To ensure consistency with supervisory practice, we align the tree construction process with liquidity-horizonspecific risk factors defined by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. We further reduce the influence of correlated covariates by proposing a methodology of cluster-wise random variable draws when building each tree. In an application to daily returns of 24 large-cap U.S. stocks from 2000 to 2023, the proposed marketdriven forecast combination delivers significantly lower out-of-sample VaR-ES losses than the standard relative-score benchmark for up to 22 out of 24 assets across multiple liquidity horizons, while also improving coverage properties and economic interpretability.

detail.abstract: Systematic option-based hedging strategies are theoretically attractive due to their convex payoff profiles but often fail in practice. The prevailing explanation attributes this failure to the negative expected returns of long options driven by volatility risk premia. This paper challenges that view by demonstrating that implementation frictions arising from option time structure play a more dominant role. Using a dynamic delta put strategy conditioned on market volatility (VIX), we compare short-dated (10 days to expiry) and mid-term (45-21 days to expiry) option structures over U.S. equity markets from 2010 to 2026. We show that short-dated strategies collapse due to excessive gamma-induced turnover and accelerated theta decay, whereas mid-term strategies achieve superior risk-adjusted returns (Sharpe 0.94 vs 0.78) by maintaining stable convex exposure primarily through vega. This advantage remains robust under conservative assumptions on transaction costs (up to 3%), volatility skew, and regime-dependent liquidity stress. Our findings suggest that for systematic hedging, selecting an appropriate option time structure is more critical than optimizing hedge ratios or rebalancing frequency.

title: The Effect of Increased Earned Income Tax Credit Generosity on Household Consumption

detail.abstract: This study examines how the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) affects household consumption. I use 1999-2019 data from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID) that includes annual spending data on a variety of disaggregated consumption categories. This expands the current literature, in which we know more about how EITC eligibility is associated with the seasonality or timing of consumption, rather than the causal relationship between policy-induced changes in EITC benefit generosity and annual consumption. I find that policy-induced increases in EITC benefits increase spending on work-related costs like childcare and transportation; big-ticket purchases like owning a vehicle; and goods and services with positive income elasticities like private health insurance, education, eating out, and trips and vacations. These overall changes in consumption speak more directly to the mechanisms through which the EITC may improve wellbeing, suggesting that increased EITC benefit generosity can both reduce stress by fostering greater mobility and ability to engage in discretionary spending, as well as increase spending on specific goods and services like education, childcare, and health that could enhance child development.

title: Real Estate Agents' Collaboration and Housing Outcomes
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU), University of Georgia - Department of Insurance, Legal Studies, Real Estate and University of Georgia - Department of Insurance, Legal Studies, Real Estate

detail.title: Real Estate Agents' Collaboration and Housing Outcomes
detail.abstract: This paper examines how collaboration between listing and selling agents influences housing market outcomes and how these effects differ across the institutional environments of conventional and foreclosure (REO) transactions. Using more than 150,000 singlefamily sales from the Dallas-Fort Worth metro area, we develop a conceptual framework describing how REO market structure can generate heterogeneous collaboration effects. We estimate jointly determined price and time-on-market (TOM) equations with detailed agent controls and distinguish between repeated interactions within specific agent pairs (depth) and broader patterns of collaborative activity (breadth). In conventional sales, neither dyad depth nor collaboration breadth materially affects prices or TOM once agent characteristics are accounted for. In the REO segment, repeated interactions beyond the first two joint sales are associated with price discounts of roughly two percent, while collaboration has little effect on TOM. Overall, the evidence indicates no meaningful collaboration effects in conventional transactions and modest, price-specific effects in the institutionally constrained REO market.

title: Modeling the Dynamics and Impact of Human-AI Interactions with Attention Transition Network Analysis
affiliations: University of Eastern Finland, , FernUniversitat in Hagen, University of Melbourne and University of Eastern Finland

detail.title: Modeling the Dynamics and Impact of Human-AI Interactions with Attention Transition Network Analysis

declarations.funderStatement: This work is co-funded by the Research Council of Finland (Suomen Akatemia) —projects CRETIC (360746) and TOPEILA (350560)— as well as by the European Commission —project ISILA (2023-1-FI01-KA220-HED-000159757).

detail.abstract: Network analysis is a well-established approach for the modeling of interactions and relationships across several domains of educational research. However, existing methods face limitations in capturing the temporal order, depth and influence within temporal data. To address these challenges, we introduce Attention Transition Network Analysis (ATNA), a temporal network framework inspired by the attention mechanism in large language models that captures temporal depth where neighboring nodes receive higher attention which decays by distance. The attention and decay can be tuned according to context. Hence, it provides a flexible framework for modeling the temporal depth of relevance. ATNA includes confirmatory testing: bootstrapping to evaluate individual edge stability, case dropping for centrality robustness testing, and permutation for comparing across different processes. Such an extensive level of confirmatory testing affords researchers rigorous mechanisms to ensure that the results of their analysis are genuinely meaningful and not artefacts within the data. In this paper, we introduce the foundations of the ATNA method, compare it to existing methods, describe its mathematical foundations, and illustrate it with a case study in modeling student-AI interactions in programming education.

title: How predictable is job destruction? Evidence from the Occupational Outlook
affiliations: Naval Postgraduate School

detail.title: How predictable is job destruction? Evidence from the Occupational Outlook
detail.abstract: Is it feasible to alert workers of impending job destruction? For 80 years, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics has tried, providing thousands of employment forecasts in its Occupational Outlook. I test accuracy by comparing these forecasts to actual job growth. The forecasts were informative: across 4,000 unique predictions, occupations in the top third of projections grew significantly more in the subsequent three decades compared to ones in the bottom third. The forecasts were especially accurate when they made reference to business practices, like how a shift to cafeteria-style restaurants decreased the demand for waiters. Technology-focused forecasts were less accurate because, on average, they underestimated the extent of job loss. While the forecasts outperform naive extrapolations, the advantage is small, indicating that most of the explanatory power is captured in pre-existing trends. Overall, these results suggest that--at least historically--occupational growth and collapse has been foreseeable.

title: Comparative Analysis of Pseudo-Random and Low-Discrepancy Number Generators: Implications for Normality and Value-at-Risk Estimation in Investment Portfolios
affiliations: Union Investment Institutional GmbH, Imperial College London - Faculty of Engineering and Institute of Information and Communication Technologies - Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
